newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slumps to six-week low vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slumps to six-week low vs basket.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased slightly on Wednesday as small foreign investor withdrawal and importer orders nudged the local currency down to its lowest level against the currency basket since late May, dealers said.
The zloty may stand to lose more ground in early Thursday as banks rebuild positions after cutting them today, but dealers said the zloty could be buoyed off lows before long.

"Many slimmed positions on Wednesday to take advantage of the weekend value date, so there may be dollar buying early on Thursday," said Tomasz Wolosz, dealer at BRE SA. "But some may think the zloty is attractive at present rates," he added.

The zloty closed at 0.69/0.66 percent above parity, against Tuesday's 0.94/0.89 finish, its lowest level since May 27, when the zloty fell to 0.35 percent above parity on the day when the neighbouring Czech crown tumbled by eight percent.
It closed at 3.3065/75 to the dollar, down from 3.2930/50 on Tuesday and at 1.8774/80 to the mark, down from 1.8760/70.

Dealers said the zloty was under downward pressure from foreign investors, who were slowly trimming Polish portfolios amid rising interest rates and virtually no hopes of zloty appreciation in the medium-term.

The central bank on Wednesday reaffirmed its Tuesday increase of the money market's benchmark 14-day reverse repo rate to 22.59 percent and one-day rates remained underpinned at this new level, dealers said.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates both closed flat at 22.30/22.60 and 22.40/22.65 percent respectively.
At today's auction the central bank drained 10 million zlotys at 22.59 and capped its 91-day maximum yield at 22.50 percent for the second straight day.
